title: UK names the vehicle for its puppy-smuggling entry ban: the European Partnership Bill
body: The UK–EU summit explainer confirms the planned ban on dogs and cats under six months old or heavily pregnant entering Great Britain will be introduced through the European Partnership Bill and secondary legislation, with tightly controlled exemptions including for genuine EU pet owners and a review after five years. No start date has been published; the ban is not in force. The Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Act 2025 already requires the first regulations under it to impose the same bans. All 30 Great Britain dog and cat route pages now carry the update in their age-and-pregnancy FAQ (the two Turkey routes, which lacked the FAQ, gained it).

body: On 20 November 2026 the UK and EU concluded the SPS agreement at their summit, and Defra's guidance 'Pet animals: preparing for changes' confirms that from 1 March 2028 owners will be able to get a multi-use pet passport valid for EU travel instead of an animal health certificate for each trip. The passport cannot be obtained yet and cannot be used until 1 March 2028 — until then an AHC is still required for every GB to EU trip. The same guidance changes the non-commercial limit into Great Britain from 5 pets per person to 5 per vehicle, or 5 per foot passenger. The 1 March 2028 date applies 'subject to UK and EU procedures', and the full treaty text is still unpublished — the published record is the joint statement (EU Council document ST 16174/26) plus the GOV.UK explainers.

United Kingdom: the 2025 import Act is law but not yet in force — under-6-month and late-pregnancy bans still to come
body: The Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Act 2025 (c. 30) received Royal Assent on 2 December 2025. Section 1(3)-(4) requires the first regulations made under it for England, Scotland and Wales to prohibit bringing in dogs or cats below the age of 6 months, dogs or cats more than 42 days pregnant, and mutilated animals. Those operative provisions are not yet in force — no commencement regulations have been made — so today's GB entry rules are unchanged and the current minimum age stays at about 15 weeks. All 29 of our Great Britain inbound dog, cat and ferret pages carry this warning in their FAQs; this entry records the position in the change log. We will update the affected pages the day a commencement date is set.

title: Chile: permanent ID now mandatory for dogs, cats and ferrets from 27 July 2026
body: Under SAG Exempt Resolution No. 3,343 (published 28 April 2026, in force 27 July 2026, repealing Resolution 6,508/2021), dogs, cats and ferrets entering Chile need permanent identification — an ISO 11784/11785 microchip or a tattoo, with the number matching the CVI. First rabies vaccination at least 21 days before entry; clinical exam within 10 days before the CVI is issued, and antiparasitic treatment 5 to 30 days before it; CVI valid 10 days, extendable by 5. No rabies antibody test, no advance permit and no quarantine. US to Chile dog and cat pages went live on 20 November 2026.

title: Vietnam: new pet import circular in force from 1 January 2026
body: Circular 01/2026/TT-BNNMT (Ministry of Agriculture and Environment) replaces Circular 25/2016. Owners travelling with one or two dogs or cats declare them at the airport border quarantine post; the import quarantine certificate (Form 15a) is issued within one working day if no sampling is needed. Three or more pets need advance approval from the Department of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Medicine. Microchip before rabies vaccination. From 1 August 2026, Decree 204 fines walking a dog in public without a muzzle or leash at 1 to 2 million dong. US to Vietnam dog and cat pages went live on 20 November 2026.

title: Philippines: rabies titer test and new Form 1 required for import permits from 1 January 2027
body: Under BAI Memorandum Circular No. 60 (26 October 2026), SPSIC applications for dogs and cats approved from 1 January 2027 must include a rabies neutralizing antibody titer result of at least 0.5 IU/ml from a government-accredited laboratory and a completed Form 1 per animal. Rabies becomes the only required vaccine and the minimum age at application is 18 weeks. We had no Philippines-inbound pages, so we built the US to Philippines dog and cat pages on the new rules rather than patching anything.

title: EU entry certificates: new official form mandatory for certificates issued from 1 October 2026
body: Under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, animal health certificates for pets entering the EU must follow the new model (Part 1 of Annex III). Certificates issued on the old model (Part 1 of Annex IV to Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) before 1 October 2026 remain acceptable only if the pet is presented at the border by 31 March 2027. The affected route pages now carry this as a question, with the EUR-Lex text as the source.

body: Japan's Animal Quarantine Service (AQS) suspended, in principle, the import quarantine procedures for dogs and cats exported from Kyrgyzstan on 12 June 2026; the suspension is still in force. title: Singapore: from 1 April 2026, an AVS-recognised agent must run arrival clearance at Changi
body: AVS has confirmed that from 1 April 2026 only AVS-recognised pet agents may handle import clearance at the Changi Animal and Plant Quarantine Station (CAPQ) — owners must appoint an agent before arrival and can no longer enter the Changi Airfreight Centre themselves. The agent also handles the onward transport home for pets that do not need quarantine. The pet licence, import licence application and inspection booking remain the owner's own steps, and veterinary documents are still prepared by the owner and their vet. The four Singapore route pages now carry the new clearance step.

title: New Zealand's 2026 cat and dog rules: titer window shortens, ID check starts 1 October 2026
body: MPI's 2026 import health standard for cats and dogs (issued 12 May 2026) runs alongside the 2021 standard until 1 April 2027, when it becomes the only one. For Category 3 origins (including the US and UK): the RNATT sample window shortens from 3–24 months to 3–12 months before shipment; a pre-export identification check becomes mandatory from 1 October 2026; dogs gain a lungworm treatment within 5 days of shipment, a Babesia rossi declaration for dogs never in mainland Africa, and a Leishmania infantum test; cats need one external parasite treatment instead of two. The four affected route pages have been updated to the 2026 rules.

title: Nobivac NXT Rabies vaccine no longer accepted for Great Britain
body: USDA APHIS reports (page updated 19 November 2026) that the Nobivac NXT Rabies vaccine — Merck's new RNA-particle rabies vaccine, launched in the US in November 2026 — no longer meets UK vaccine requirements; pets arriving vaccinated with it are treated as non-compliant, and Heathrow's Animal Reception Centre is reviewing pets due to arrive. GOV.UK requires an inactivated or recombinant rabies vaccine, and the UK authorised-products list has no NXT rabies vaccine for Great Britain. If your pet was vaccinated with Nobivac NXT, revaccinate with an accepted vaccine and restart the 21-day wait.

title: United Kingdom: two new H5N1 cases in England; first Northern Ireland case
body: GOV.UK confirms H5N1 in commercial poultry near Coningsby, Lincolnshire (AIV 2026/30) and near Thirsk, North Yorkshire (AIV 2026/31), both on 18 November 2026, each with a 3 km protection zone and 10 km surveillance zone. The 2026–27 season total is now 12 H5N1 cases: 9 in England, 2 in Scotland, 1 in Northern Ireland. Northern Ireland's first case was confirmed near Coagh, County Londonderry on 16 November 2026, and its Avian Influenza Prevention Zone takes effect at 00:01 on 19 November 2026 (mandatory housing, gatherings ban); Wales joined the prevention zone from midday on 16 November 2026 (biosecurity only).

The season's latest confirmed H5N1 case was in backyard poultry near Stromness, Orkney (AIV 2026/29), and England's season total stands at 7 cases. Great Britain's zone-based position for US-bound birds is unchanged — what matters is whether the bird has been inside a current protection or surveillance zone.
